text:
eli: Heads up — intermittent DNS failures for a statefulset in edge-us-east when GPU pool autoscaler drains nodes. Headless service resolves to no endpoints for ~20-40s, apps hit NXDOMAIN or empty SRV. SNAT metrics on the NAT gateway spike during drains. Any ideas?

sara: Can you paste the coreDNS + endpointslice controller logs you saw?

eli: coreDNS shows repeated lookups failing: 
```
[ERROR] lookup mydb.default.svc.cluster.local. on 10.0.0.10:53: server can't find mydb.default.svc.cluster.local: NXDOMAIN
```
endpointslice controller logs show transient updates like: `Failed to update EndpointSlice: conflict` but the slices exist; `kubectl get endpointslices -n default -o wide` intermittently shows slice with zero endpoints for the statefulset.

jon: Sounds like something clearing or blocking endpoint traffic during the drain. Which kube-proxy mode are those nodes running (ipvs/iptables/BPF)? Could be conntrack / SNAT exhaustion.

eli: Nodes are on iptables mode (we never moved them to BPF in that pool). Also saw kube-proxy sync warnings: `E1001 12:34:56.789 kube-proxy.go:412] sync failed: failed to ensure iptables rules: xtables lock held`

ashley: Are we using NAT gateways for egress in that AZ? MetalLB not in play for egress, this is AWS NAT GW. If nat gw runs out of SNAT ports we get asymmetric traffic.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-348 — NAT gateway SNAT high allocation (auto-detected).

sara: Check conntrack counts on nodes: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` and `nf_conntrack_max`. Also `kubectl logs` for endpointslice-controller for any rate-limited errors.

eli: Ran checks: `nf_conntrack_count=124300` `nf_conntrack_max=131072` on a few nodes. `conntrack -S` shows peaks aligned with drain events.

jon: That lines up with SNAT / conntrack exhaustion. When conntrack fills, new flows fail and return packets can be dropped, leading to short windows where kube-proxy/EndpointSlice updates race with failing dataplane. Two mitigations: increase nf_conntrack_max and reduce egress burst (or add more NAT capacity). Also consider switching to kube-proxy BPF on newer nodes to reduce xtables lock contention.

ashley: Immediate mitigation options: (1) scale nat-gateway or add a secondary NAT in same subnet, (2) stagger drains to avoid big simultaneous egress bursts, (3) bump conntrack on nodes. Which is fastest?

eli: I spun up an extra small NAT GW in the subnet and added SNAT mapping to the route table for the node subnet. Will watch metrics.

jon: Also will test a small pool with kube-proxy in ipvs->bpf or at least ipvs tuning, and add a quick check to the draining workflow so we don't evict many GPU pods at once (they upload checkpoints and trigger huge egress).

ashley: Filing a follow-up: INFRA-987 to: adjust autoscaler drain rate, add pre-drain hook to pause checkpoint uploads, and permanently provision a dedicated egress for draining nodes.

eli: Update ~25m after extra NAT: SNAT allocation dropped, conntrack count fell ~30k, headless service endpoints returned immediately, DNS resolution stabilized. Looks like the main trigger was bursty egress during GPU pod termination (model checkpoints hitting S3) combined with conntrack limits and xtables lock contention delaying kube-proxy reconciliation.

sara: Great root cause summary. Can we add a proactive alert: NAT SNAT utilization > 70% and nf_conntrack_count > 80% thresholds, and include a runbook that lists quick mitigations (add NAT, throttle drains, bump nf_conntrack_max, migrate to BPF)?

jon: I'll draft the runbook and a small playbook change to the autoscaler to add a 2-min grace period before eviction for GPU jobs.

ashley: Thumbs up. Also add a Redwood Optimize check to flag workloads that upload >X MB per termination event. That'll help prevent recurrence. :thumbsup:

eli: Thanks everyone — closing this thread, will post the runbook link when it's ready.
